title: Heuristic review lab notebook — Hiral
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy notebook for review heuristics and micro-experiments. Personal scratchpad — keep small, keep actionable. Mostly for PR triage / follow-ups for serving runtime and small refactors.

Context notes (TL;DR):
- Frequent review pain points: hidden perf regressions, test flakiness in CI, unclear rollback surface, ambiguous ownership for low-level cache changes.
- Goal: build a short checklist + small hypothesis-driven experiments to run when a review touches hotpath (batching, kv-cache, kernel selection).

Quick review checklist (starter, use/adapt per-PR):
- Scope sanity: does the PR touch hot-path code (batching, kv-cache, tokenization, attention loops)? If yes -> escalate to SRE/Perf reviewer.
- Safety nets: are feature flags added for behavior changes? If not, is the change small enough to risk?
- Tests: unit + perf microbenchmark included? If no perf test, add a minimal harness that reproduces pre/post metric (latency P95, token throughput).
- Observability: added metrics/traces? (latency hist, cache hit/miss counters, batch-size distribution)
- Backwards compat: any wire-format or API surface change? Is migration plan documented?
- Rollback path: quick revert + fallback model variant? Validate fallback path in staging.
- Owners: who signs off on perf risks? Call out explicitly in PR description.

Heuristic signals I eyeball in diffs (fast scan):
- Loops with extra allocations (new array/map inside hot loop).
- Synchronous logging in hot-path code (log.warn inside token gen loop).
- Unnecessary locking around read-only state.
- New serialization/deserialization steps on request path.
- Small changes that modify ordering of ops near KV cache lookup.

My quick experiment recipes (to run locally / quick CI):
1) Minimal perf harness: compile with perf flags, run 10k short sequences and record P95. Example runner: `scripts/mini_perf_runner --model gpt-small --seq 128 --iters 10000`
2) KV-cache microtest: instrument cache hit/miss counters and run repeated prefix requests of length 64/96/128 to observe hit-rate. Compare before/after PR.
3) Batch-distribution test: simulate concurrent 200 req/s with synthetic shapes, capture distribution of batch sizes (shouldn't collapse to 1s).

Refactor ideas to reduce review friction (notes to self):
- Move small helper functions out of hot-path file to reduce diff noise in actual critical loop.
- Introduce a thin immutable wrapper around KV cache so read-only callers avoid locks. (Prototype: KVReadView)
- Standardize perf microbench harness in `./bench` and require a tiny perf script for PRs touching runtime.

Risk matrix shorthand (for triage):
- Low risk: documentation, comments, tests only -> review by 1 engineer.
- Medium risk: refactors not touching hot-path but touching shared types -> 2 reviewers + run unit perf harness.
- High risk: any change in batching, kv-cache, kernel selection, or traceable latency path -> 2 reviewers (incl. perf), perf bench + staged canary.

Follow-ups to log on PRs (copy into checklist comment on merge):
- Post-merge: run `mini_perf_runner` in staging for 24h and capture baseline vs current (store results in perf-results/).
- Add an automated GitHub Action that runs the mini perf for PRs labeled `perf-check` (budgeted runs; sample size 200).
- If cache hit-rate drops >5% for top-10 prefixes, trigger alert for rollback.

Notes on recent PR (for context) — PR 4128 (linked above):
- Changes: alter cache eviction policy and add adaptive sampling.
- My initial read: adaptive code paths add extra branching inside lookup; could increase branch mispredictions.
- Immediate action: request perf harness + microbench; add metric for branch-exit counts.
- Unresolved: does eviction change affect multitenant fairness? Add tenancy-tagged metrics.

Checklist for creating small perf tests (TODO template):
- [ ] Identify minimal request shape that hits code path
- [ ] Create harness args (model, seq, batch parallelism)
- [ ] Add baseline run script (commit baseline before PR change)
- [ ] Add comparison job (post-merge or PR-run)
- [ ] Save artifacts (json/csv) and link from PR description

Common friction that keeps coming up in reviews:
- PR descriptions assume reviewers know the perf baseline — include explicit numbers.
- Test flakiness in GH Actions under contention. Might need a dedicated perf runner in staging infra.
- Ownership ambiguity: add `perf-owner` label for PRs touching runtime.

Random micro-hacks worth trying later: (brain dump)
- Bake a small `--hotpath` compile tag to compile hot-path as a single translation unit for better inlining during benching.
- Implement a `perf-smoke` GH Action that runs on a cheap instance but returns a rough P95 delta. Not authoritative but quick signal.

Stuff to iterate with Avery/Jonah:
- Avery: help with writing the perf runner wrapper and GH Action.
- Jonah: sketch out metrics to add to kv-cache (per-model + per-tenant hit-rate).

Open questions (need answers before finalizing checklist):
- How many PRs touching cache actually caused regressions historically? (ask infra-sre for postmortem list)
- Acceptable perf delta budget for small changes — is 2% P95 allowed or 5%? Need a documented SLO.

Notes-to-self (short-term tasks):
- [ ] Draft a PR template snippet to force perf rationale + quick bench output.
- [ ] Run PR4128 perf harness locally and paste results into GH PR.
- [ ] Add tenant-tagging to cache metrics (small patch).

End notes: keep this short and pragmatic. Pull whatever parts of this into PR comments/templates when relevant. If something feels too heavy, trim to 1-2 checks that are easy to run — adoption matters more than perfection.
